Beadwork persists plans, progress, and decisions to git so they survive. Compaction erases context.

Issues live on the `beadwork` branch. IDs: `tb-XYZ`. Status: open → in_progress → closed / deferred. Priority: P0-P4 (default P2). Epics have children (`--parent`) and deps (`bw dep add <blocker> blocks <blocked>`). `bw ready` feeds you the next unblocked step, so compaction can't erase your progress.

Due dates (`bw update <id> --due <date>`) are deadlines that do not change status. Deferred issues (`bw defer`) are hidden from `bw ready`; due issues are not. content.text:
Found the cause: your commits are signed by **Secretive** (`ash-key@secretive.ash.local`), which stores the SSH key in the Secure Enclave and requires you to approve each signature (Touch ID / notification). The first two commits signed fine, then an approval got denied or timed out, so now even `jj status`/`jj log` fail — they can't sign the working-copy snapshot. I've stopped retrying so I don't pile up more denied prompts.

**State is intact — nothing lost:**

| Package | Status |
|---|---|
| ✅ rust 1.97.0 | committed (`2620806`) |
| ✅ gh 2.96.0 | committed (`24eb68a`) |
| ⏳ gopls 0.23.0 | edited, built & verified, **uncommitted** (working-tree change to `packages/gopls/data.json`, vendorHash `REDACTED`) |
| ⬜ rust-analyzer, just, ty, hunk | hashes computed, not yet applied |

All the remaining hashes are already computed and cached, so once signing works I can move quickly.

**To unblock:** re-enable Secretive signing — unlock the Secretive app / re-authenticate so it will approve signature requests again (and approve the prompt when it appears). Then tell me to continue and I'll commit gopls and do the last four.

If you'd rather not deal with the per-signature approvals for this batch, say so and I can suggest alternatives (e.g. you temporarily disabling commit signing) — but I won't change your signing config myself.

content.text:
All 7 bumps are done — each landed as its own signed jj change on top of `main`, and every binary was built and version-checked on `aarch64-darwin`:

| Package | Bump | Verified |
|---|---|---|
| rust | 1.96.0 → **1.97.0** | `rustc 1.97.0`, `cargo 1.97.0` |
| gh | 2.95.0 → **2.96.0** | `gh version 2.96.0` |
| gopls | 0.22.0 → **0.23.0** | builds (source, new vendorHash) |
| rust-analyzer | 2026-06-22 → **2026-07-06** | `0.3.2963-standalone` |
| just | 1.54.0 → **1.56.0** | `just 1.56.0` |
| ty | 0.0.56 → **0.0.58** | `ty 0.0.58` |
| hunk | 0.16.0 → **0.17.0** | `hunk 0.17.0` |

All four platform hashes were computed for each prebuilt package (not just the local one), so the entries are complete for reproducible cross-system builds. The registry evaluates cleanly with the new defaults.

Two notes:

- **`nix flake check` fails on an unrelated devenv check** (`devenv was not able to determine the current directory` — a known devenv-with-flakes quirk). It's pre-existing and independent of these edits, which only touch `data.json`. I verified my changes instead via `nix eval` on the registry (output above) — all seven defaults are correct.
- **Toolchains still pin the old versions.** Meta-packages like `rust-toolchain`, `go-toolchain` (pins gopls), and `python-toolchain` (pins ty) reference specific tool versions and were *not* touched — per the repo's pattern, bumping a toolchain is a separate, deliberate version-increment commit. Want me to roll these into new toolchain versions, or leave the toolchains as-is?

There were also pre-existing beadwork tickets for other bumps (biome, ruff, nix, mdbook-mermaid, mdbook-graphviz, golangci-lint, nodejs, mdbook-footnote) — I left those alone since they weren't in your list. Happy to take any of them next.
